label: Resonator spectroscopy
axes: A per-entity panel grid (one small panel per readout resonator, each titled with its entity name). In the main "amplitude + fit" figure the horizontal axis is the swept readout drive frequency, with a second axis along the top repeating the same sweep as detuning from the previously stored value; the vertical axis is demodulated readout magnitude R = sqrt(I^2 + Q^2). Each panel carries a solid measured trace and a dashed fitted resonance model; the claimed resonance is the dashed model's minimum (in the wide-sweep variant the claim is instead a single vertical dashed marker drawn over a baseline-subtracted magnitude trace). Two companion figures share the same panel layout: a "phase" figure (same horizontal axis, vertical axis = demodulated phase, measured trace only, no fit) and an "IQ circle" figure (I on the horizontal axis vs Q on the vertical, one dot per swept point colored by drive frequency, with a star marking the claimed resonance).
correct_signature: Exactly one downward excursion dominates the panel: it is the deepest AND the narrowest feature in the trace, and its depth is several times the point-to-point scatter of the trace away from it.

The dip is resolved, not a glitch — its descent and its recovery each span several consecutive sweep points and the bottom is rounded, so the notch shape is drawn by many points rather than one or two.

The dashed model overlays the measured notch: its minimum sits on the measured minimum within a fraction of the notch's own width, its width matches the measured width, and its lowest point does not go below the lowest measured point (and never below zero magnitude, which is physically impossible for R).

Away from the notch the trace returns to a smooth, slowly varying level on BOTH sides; that level may be tilted or gently curved and the flat-baselined model may sit off it in the far wings — wing-only mismatch is expected and does not disqualify a figure.
The phase companion shows a smooth, coherent excursion (a steep monotone ramp, step, or sharp cusp) whose centre lines up with the magnitude notch, riding on an otherwise smooth phase background.

The IQ companion traces a loop that closes or nearly closes, with the point colors advancing in order around it, and the claimed-resonance star lies on or beside that loop rather than isolated in empty space; several concentric loops from a broad sweep are still fine as long as one loop is ordered and closed.

Across the grid most panels look like the above; the notch may be broad or razor-narrow relative to the swept window (that is the operator's sweep choice, not a defect) so long as it is still built from multiple points.

failure_appearance.wrong_peak: The dashed model's minimum is not on the deepest, widest-supported notch. Observed form: the model latches onto a single-sample vertical glitch (in one panel an UPWARD spike) and draws a needle there, while the genuine shallow, many-point dip sits untouched elsewhere in the same trace. Other checkable forms: the model centred on a trough of the slow baseline ripple while a much deeper narrow notch sits more than a couple of its own widths away; or the model parked on the shoulder of a monotone slope with no notch under it at all. Judge on relative geometry only — being far from any drawn feature is what matters, never where in the window it sits.
failure_appearance.no_signal: The whole panel is hash: excursions of roughly equal size scattered everywhere, none deeper or wider than its neighbours, no place the trace settles to a smooth level. The phase companion is equally jagged with no smooth monotone excursion anywhere. The fitter's response is a tell — on several such panels no dashed curve is drawn at all, and where one is drawn it is a needle plunging far below every measured point (in the strongest case below zero magnitude). This was the dominant character of the rejected exemplar.
failure_appearance.noisy: The notch is there but only just: scatter is a large fraction of the notch depth, the bottom is defined by a couple of points, the recovery on one or both sides is ragged rather than smooth, and the dashed model's width is visibly wider than the run of points that actually define the notch. The phase excursion is still discernible but jagged rather than clean. Correct verdict is reduced confidence, not automatic rejection — accepted exemplars include noticeably noisy panels whose notch still dominates its own scatter.
failure_appearance.drifted: These figures carry no repeat or time axis, so a resonance moving between repeats cannot be seen. The only visible proxy observed is a mid-sweep change in the trace's character — one stretch carrying a large regular ripple butting straight onto a flat, low-scatter stretch, i.e. acquisition conditions not constant across the sweep. Treat this as a caution flag only when the claim sits near that boundary; it appeared in a figure the node accepted, and it is confounded with segmented acquisition, so it is not on its own a rejection.
failure_appearance.feature_present_fit_failed: A clear, well-supported notch is visible in the measured trace and the dashed model does not describe it: the model is drawn as a needle far narrower than the measured notch and descends past the bottom of the data (sometimes clear off the bottom of the panel or below zero magnitude, impossible for a magnitude); or the model is essentially flat while an obvious notch sits under it; or the model's depth is a small fraction of the measured depth. Observed in both the rejected run and in isolated panels of accepted runs. Distinguish this from the benign case where the model tracks the notch faithfully and only misses the tilted or rippled wings — that one is normal.

abstain_when: The sweep is broad enough that the notch would be narrower than the plotted line — the trace reads as flat or uniformly rippled everywhere and the only mark of the claim is a vertical line with nothing resolvable under it. This is the wide-sweep variant's normal appearance and it is NOT evidence of a wrong peak; ask for a zoomed panel instead of guessing.
The figure is a per-entity grid and it cannot be determined which panel the numeric claim refers to — the claim names an entity absent from every panel title, or the panel titles are unreadable.
No fit overlay and no marker is drawn on the panel in question, so the claim cannot be located on the picture at all.
Two or more downward features are comparable in both depth and point-support and sit far apart, so the picture alone cannot rank them; the phase or IQ companion is needed to break the tie.

The trace has been baseline-subtracted or otherwise transformed (axis centred on zero, a large regular ripple dominating) so that depth relative to a baseline and the notch's own scatter can no longer be read off the picture.
notes: Evidence base is thin and worth stating: three accepted runs (two narrow per-entity sweeps, one wide baseline-subtracted sweep with its IQ companion) and one rejected run, read as seven images total. Maintainer-critical points: (1) These are PER-ENTITY grids and the node's accept/reject is per entity, so accepted figures demonstrably contain individually broken panels — never condemn a whole figure because one panel's fit is a needle. Judge the panel the claim names. (2) The single largest false-reject risk is wing mismatch: the fitted model carries a flat baseline while real traces ride a tilted, curved or rippled background from the readout line, so a model that hugs the notch and diverges from the data in the far wings is a GOOD figure, and this pattern is present in nearly every accepted panel. (3) One hard, unit-free physical check is available: the plotted quantity is a magnitude, so any part of the dashed model dipping below zero is decisive evidence the fit is unphysical. (4) In everything read, resonance appears as a DIP in magnitude; if a future run plots the resonance as a peak, the depth/width/support reasoning transfers but the judge should say so rather than silently inverting. (5) The rejected exemplar differed from the accepted ones mainly by the measured signal collapsing to structureless hash; a judge who cannot see absolute scales must reach that conclusion from 'no feature dominates its own scatter' plus 'the fitter drew nothing, or drew a needle outside the data', which were both plainly visible. (6) The phase companion was the cleanest single discriminator in this sample — smooth coherent excursion on accepted panels, undifferentiated jitter on rejected ones — so request it when the amplitude panel is borderline. (7) The wide-sweep variant supplies only a vertical marker over a segment-median-subtracted trace and should be treated as weak evidence for or against a claim.
